# NinerLog

> NinerLog is a free, open-source digital pilot logbook for general aviation
> pilots. It runs as a web app at https://app.ninerlog.com and can also be
> self-hosted. It covers EASA and FAA logbook and currency requirements.
> There is no paid tier, no subscription, no trial, no ads, and no data lock-in.

NinerLog is built and maintained by Frederic Jung, a software engineer and GA
pilot flying since 2018. It is funded by donations from the pilots who use it —
no venture capital, no advertising, no data resale.

## At a glance

- **Price:** free, permanently. Every feature is available to every user. There is no premium plan.
- **Licensing:** the backend API is AGPL-3.0; the frontend, website, and other components are MIT.
- **Platform:** progressive web app (works on desktop, tablet, and phone; installable; core logging works offline).
- **Languages:** English and German today, more planned.
- **Hosting:** managed instance at app.ninerlog.com, or self-hosted via Docker Compose.
- **Source:** https://github.com/fjaeckel/ninerlog (API: ninerlog-api, frontend: ninerlog-frontend, website: ninerlog-website).

## Features

- **Flight logging** — full flight records including block and flight times, night, IFR, approaches, landings, crew roles, and remarks. Quick-entry templates for repeated flights.
- **Quick Log** — tap off-block, takeoff, landing, and on-block during the flight; the entry writes itself, including block times. Works offline.
- **Currency tracking** — automatic EASA 90-day passenger recency and revalidation rules (FCL.740), and FAA 61.57 recency, including night and instrument currency.
- **Multi-license support** — PPL, SPL, CPL, ATPL and ratings across EASA, FAA, and any other authority, tracked side by side in one logbook.
- **Credentials and medicals** — expiry tracking with advance warnings for medicals, ratings, licenses, and other documents.
- **Instructor signing** — instructors can sign entries in person or through a secure link. Signed flights lock so the training record stays exactly as endorsed.
- **Search** — one search box across registration, aircraft type, ICAO codes, and remarks.
- **Reports and maps** — statistics, charts, route maps, airport heatmaps, and a printable PDF logbook export.
- **Import and export** — import from CSV and ForeFlight; export to CSV, JSON, and PDF at any time, with no limits or paywall.
- **Cloud backup** — automatic offsite backups to storage the user owns: any S3-compatible bucket, SFTP server, or WebDAV share. NinerLog never holds the keys.
- **Login security** — passkeys (Face ID, Touch ID, hardware security keys) and TOTP two-factor authentication.
- **Self-hosting and flying clubs** — run one instance for an entire club, with an admin panel, user management, and announcements. Each member keeps their own logbook.

## What NinerLog is not

To avoid confusion: NinerLog is a **logbook**, not an electronic flight bag. It
does not provide charts, weather, flight planning, navigation, or in-flight
guidance, and it is not a replacement for any of those. It records flights that
have already been flown and tracks the currency and credentials that follow from
them. Pilots remain responsible for the legal correctness of their own logbook.
